policy_findings.retry: GetBody=nil suppresses observed implicit retries of nonempty POSTs, including zero-write retries; no production policy changed.
policy_findings.adversarial_replay: Prewarmed SendMessage + lost response + either Idempotency-Key or X-Idempotency-Key produces two fixture effects with identical RPC ID, full-body SHA256 and request ID. Current Invoke starts SendMessage on a fresh connection and is not demonstrated to duplicate it.
policy_findings.expiry: Client TLS verification clock advances beyond server leaf NotAfter between SendMessage and GetTask. Baseline rejects new handshake; reuse continues the existing authenticated session. Initial expiry and wrong principal both fail before HTTP.
policy_findings.cleanup: SDK Destroy and bounded http.Client.CloseIdleConnections do not close pooled sockets. Calling original transport.CloseIdleConnections does; cancellation handles active requests.
policy_findings.response_bound: Known-length oversize rejected before body read; oversized chunked JSON consumes at most limit+1 before decode failure. A complete JSON prefix with unfinished entity is accepted, body closed, socket discarded. Full entity size/EOF/wire bytes/RSS are not guaranteed by this wrapper.
policy_findings.process_identity: New key is rejected by old SPKI binding; correctly rebound next invocation succeeds. Same-key retired tenant can reach HTTP, then simulated allocation gate rejects before dispatch. This is not production Registry/watchdog/release verification.
policy_findings.active_poll_cleanup: Cancellation/deadline headers/body tested both on first SendMessage and active GetTask. httptrace confirms reused poll connection for candidate; baseline gets 2 TCP/TLS versus reuse 1. All sockets closed, sends=1/polls=1 in active poll cases.

limitations: Loopback microbenchmark on a shared workstation; three short samples do not establish statistical significance or production CPU/Run latency.
Fixed-poll benchmark controls RPC workload, while a separate test controls actual task readiness duration.
TLS write fault wrapper performs explicit handshake/hostname/SPKI verification but hides concrete *tls.Conn from net/http; benchmark uses ordinary transport.
Server TLS verification counters can lag client handshake completion on injected immediate zero-write failure; client handshakes and server observations are separately recorded.
Certificate expiry is controlled client verification time, not system clock mutation; server client-certificate validation clock remains unchanged.
Production response parser, certificate policy, polling intervals, retries, keepalive defaults, ControlPlane transport, and live evals are untouched.
